title: 2nd Abyss And The Means For Escaping 1st Matter The Narrow Minds Denial Of Grandeur And The Impossibility Of Unbelief

questions.question: What can happen to a person’s mind when it gets busy only with sin, carelessness, or just the physical world?
questions.answer: It can become small and unable to understand big truth.

questions.question: What kinds of big things are hard for that narrowed mind to understand?
questions.answer: Very great and endless matters of faith.

questions.question: When such people cannot understand these great truths, what do they rush toward?
questions.answer: They rush toward rejecting and denying.

questions.question: Why do they fall into wrong belief, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Their minds and hearts are too weak and dried up to hold these deep truths.

questions.question: If they really looked at their wrong belief, what would they notice?
questions.answer: They would see that it contains many foolish and impossible ideas.

questions.question: How is belief shown in comparison to unbelief?
questions.answer: Belief is shown as fitting, sensible, and needed.

questions.question: What example is given about a person who refuses Allah’s necessary and eternal being and His perfect qualities?
questions.answer: He may wrongly spread those special qualities across countless beings or atoms.

questions.question: What is another very foolish choice mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: A person may even deny his own existence and the world’s existence.

questions.question: What helps the truths of belief and Islam stay safe from foolish ideas?
questions.answer: Their greatness and loftiness help protect them.

questions.question: Where do the truths of belief settle in a good way?
questions.answer: In sound hearts and straight minds.

questions.question: What attitude helps a person receive these truths?
questions.answer: Humble submission and sincere acceptance.

questions.question: What is this part mainly warning about?
questions.answer: It warns about falling into unbelief because of narrow thinking.

questions.question: What makes some minds narrow in this passage?
questions.answer: Forgetting Allah, doing sins, and focusing only on material things.

questions.question: How do some people act when they feel proud of the little they know?
questions.answer: They quickly reject what they cannot fully understand.

questions.question: Are the matters of faith described as tiny and simple or vast and deep?
questions.answer: They are vast and deep.

questions.question: What is said about the hearts of people who reject these truths?
questions.answer: Their hearts are spoiled and spiritually lifeless.

questions.question: Compared with belief, what is hidden inside unbelief?
questions.answer: Many absurd and impossible claims.

questions.question: What does the passage say has strongly shown this truth?
questions.answer: It says this truth has been shown very clearly and firmly.

questions.question: If someone rejects Allah’s greatness because it seems too grand, what wrong path might he take?
questions.answer: He might give Allah’s special qualities to endless created things.

questions.question: Why is that path unreasonable?
questions.answer: Because it puts what belongs to Allah onto countless weak created things.

questions.question: What extreme example is mentioned about some people’s denial?
questions.answer: They may deny themselves and the whole universe.

questions.question: What do the truths of Islam avoid?
questions.answer: They avoid dark ignorance, silly superstitions, and shocking nonsense.

questions.question: What kind of people can carry these truths well?
questions.answer: People with healthy hearts and honest, balanced minds.

questions.question: What is the “Second Abyss” about in this passage?
questions.answer: It is about the danger of slipping into unbelief and misguidance.

questions.question: What three things can trap a person’s understanding and make it too narrow?
questions.answer: Neglecting Allah, sin, and being stuck only on material things.

questions.question: Why can’t such a person understand the biggest faith questions?
questions.answer: Because those questions are too wide and deep for a cramped mind.

questions.question: What bad result comes when a person cannot fit the truths of faith into his limited thinking?
questions.answer: He may fall into denial and wrong guidance.

questions.question: Does the passage describe unbelief as wise and strong or as full of problems?
questions.answer: It describes it as full of problems.

questions.question: What would a person see if he examined his unbelief carefully?
questions.answer: He would see many impossible and senseless parts in it.

questions.question: What is one wrong idea a denier might accept about Allah’s unique qualities?
questions.answer: He might think those qualities belong to countless other beings.

questions.question: What do the truths of belief rest on in this passage?
questions.answer: They rest on greatness and loftiness.

questions.question: What do these truths escape from?
questions.answer: They escape absurd ideas, false tales, and dark ignorance.

questions.question: How do these truths enter a person properly?
questions.answer: Through full acceptance and humble surrender.

questions.question: What happens to understanding when a person lives in heedlessness and sin?
questions.answer: Understanding shrinks and cannot grasp big spiritual truths.

questions.question: What kind of matters are described as too great for that shrunken understanding?
questions.answer: Lofty, huge, and endless matters.

questions.question: What mistake do people make when they trust their little bit of knowledge too much?
questions.answer: They become proud and start denying.

questions.question: When unbelief is compared with belief, which one matches reason better?
questions.answer: Belief matches reason better.

questions.question: What is one impossible idea mentioned as part of unbelief?
questions.answer: Giving Allah’s eternal and necessary qualities to unlimited creatures.

questions.question: What other impossible idea is mentioned?
questions.answer: Denying your own existence and the world’s existence.

questions.question: Why are these examples important in the passage?
questions.answer: They show that unbelief can be more unreasonable than the truths it rejects.

questions.question: What protects the truths of faith from silly and dark mistakes?
questions.answer: Their true greatness and high rank protect them.

questions.question: What must a person show in order to receive these truths rightly?
questions.answer: Submission and agreement from the heart and mind.

questions.question: In what kind of hearts do these truths settle?
questions.answer: In healthy hearts.

questions.question: In what kind of minds do these truths settle?
questions.answer: In upright and clear minds.

questions.question: What is the first big problem described in this passage?
questions.answer: Some people’s minds become too narrow for the truths of faith.

questions.question: What causes that narrowness?
questions.answer: Neglect of Allah, sins, and being tied only to the material world.

questions.question: What do these people do because of pride in their limited knowledge?
questions.answer: They hurry to reject what is beyond them.

questions.question: What is wrong with their minds and hearts in the passage?
questions.answer: Their minds are cramped, and their hearts are corrupted and spiritually dead.

questions.question: If they could truly see their unbelief, what would they find inside it?
questions.answer: A lot of nonsense and impossibility.

questions.question: What kind of things are found in belief instead?
questions.answer: Things that are proper, reasonable, and necessary.

questions.question: What mistaken move does a denier make with Allah’s special attributes?
questions.answer: He gives them to endless beings or tiny particles.

questions.question: Why is that a worse problem than accepting Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: Because it makes creation carry what only Allah can have.

questions.question: What foolish group is mentioned as denying both self and world?
questions.answer: Some people who reject reason so far that they deny both.

questions.question: What do belief and Islam leave behind and rise above?
questions.answer: They rise above superstition, absurdity, and ignorance.

questions.question: How do the truths of belief come into a person?
questions.answer: By strong acceptance and willing surrender.

questions.question: What does the passage say about minds that are swallowed up by worldly things?
questions.answer: They become too limited to understand the greatness of faith.

questions.question: Besides the material world, what two other things help cause this problem?
questions.answer: Sin and neglect of Allah.

questions.question: What do people often do when they cannot fully understand a great truth?
questions.answer: They deny it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the size of faith questions?
questions.answer: They are very broad, deep, and all-encompassing.

questions.question: What happens to people with dried-up minds and dead hearts?
questions.answer: They fall into unbelief and go astray.

questions.question: What would careful thinking show them about unbelief?
questions.answer: It would show them that unbelief holds many impossible ideas.

questions.question: What is one example of that impossibility?
questions.answer: Saying many beings or atoms have what belongs only to Allah.

questions.question: What is another example of extreme denial?
questions.answer: Refusing to admit even yourself and the universe exist.

questions.question: According to the passage, are the truths of belief weak or strong?
questions.answer: They are strong and firmly based.

questions.question: What do these truths escape from?
questions.answer: They escape terrible foolishness, false superstitions, and dark not-knowing.

questions.question: What two places are ready to receive these truths?
questions.answer: Good hearts and straight minds.
